text:
Alice M (SRE): Heads-up — received an SLO burn alert for `api-read` (burn_rate ~3x) over the last 10m. I can't find a single-pane view that ties the SLO -> traces -> logs for this: where's the canonical starting point for triage? Need to identify root cause before paging.

Ben K: Start at the SLO overview dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/slo-overview. Click the `api-read` row, then the "Related Panels" link will jump to error-rate and latency breakdowns. Traces live in Tempo (https://tempo.redwood.internal/), logs in Loki (https://logs.redwood.internal/explore). Quick Loki snippet to narrow 5xxs in the last 10m: 

```
{job=\"ingress\", service=\"api\"} |= "5xx" | unwrap | count_over_time(10m)
```

Ben K: If you want to correlate to traces, use this Tempo/Jaeger filter: `service:api operation:handleRequest error:true duration>200ms` and look for repeated upstream timeouts.

Chris L: I checked spans for the timeframe Ben mentioned — seeing a cluster of `upstream_timeout` spans pinned to region `eu-west-1` and a handful of long DNS lookups. Could be an infra/network blip or a noisy client causing backlog.

Dana R: I'll take the lead on triage. @Alice M (SRE) can you paste the alert URL and the exact alert rule? I'll correlate with deploys and LB metrics.

sre-bot: ALERT: SLO `api-read` burn_rate > 2.0 for 10m. Triggered at 2026-03-17T15:14:38Z. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-20345.

Alice M (SRE): Alert rule: `slo:api-read:burn_rate{env=\"prod\"} > 2 for 10m`. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-20345. No deploys in the last 30m (checked CI webhooks). Metrics show error spike concentrated in eu-west-1 -> 10m spike on 5xx.

Ben K: If it's region-scoped, check the regional ingress autoscaler and the NAT gateway logs. Also grep for repeated client IPs in logs: 

```
{job=\"ingress\", region=\"eu-west-1\", service=\"api\"} | json | ip | count_over_time(10m)
```

Ben K: If you find a noisy client, we can add a short-term rate-limit rule at the LB to reduce SLO churn.

Chris L: Found ~3k requests from a handful of IP ranges hitting a deprecated endpoint with malformed headers. They cause our router to retry upstream which surfaces as 5xx. I filtered one example trace: `traceID: 8a4f3c` shows 30ms header parsing then 500 from upstream because of malformed auth.

Dana R: Okay I'll open a quick mitigation PR: add a 429 for malformed headers at the nginx ingress and a short-lived LB filter for the noisy IP ranges. I'll also propose changing the alert to include a short recovery window so transient scans don't immediately blow the burn rate: proposed alert change -> `slo:api-read:burn_rate > 2 for 15m`. Will include rationale in the PR. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3145 (WIP).

Alice M (SRE): Sounds good. Can we also add a dashboard panel that links from the SLO row directly into a pre-filtered Loki + Tempo query (region + slo tag)? That would cut triage time.

Ben K: Agreed — I'll add a Grafana panel with a template var for `slo` + `region` and a direct Tempo link. Will follow up with the panel JSON in the PR.

Dana R: For immediate runbook steps: 1) mute the alert for 20m once mitigation is live, 2) apply LB filter, 3) deploy nginx rule, 4) confirm burn rate drops and unmute. I'll update the runbook with the exact Loki/Tempo queries we used.

Chris L: FYI I added a short Nginx snippet to return 429 for the malformed header pattern: 

```nginx
if ($http_x_custom_header = "") {
  return 429;
}
```

Alice M (SRE): Thanks all. Dana — post back here when the PR is ready and after you unmute. Also please add the new dashboard link to the SLO row. :thumbsup:

Dana R: Will do. Marking as in-progress.

Ben K: Nice teamwork. Saved a noisy client from turning into a paging incident. :party_parrot:
